title: Copilot Studio: labelled and encrypted file uploads for agents on the Microsoft 365 channel
summary: The briefing accurately separates the planned labelled-upload capability from today's documented encrypted-file restriction and qualifies the existing Purview controls. The control paths, commands and ordinary usage billing are supported; the brief explanation of an agent harness needs one additional citation.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The existing file-input documentation says encrypted files, including sensitivity-labelled or password-protected files, are unsupported.
claims.quote: Files with encryption, such as sensitivity labels or password protection, aren't supported.

claims.claim: For an encrypted or password-protected Office upload, the agent can tell the user that it cannot read the file.
claims.quote: When a user uploads a password-protected or encrypted Office file, the agent tells the user that the file is encrypted or password-protected and can't be read.

claims.claim: Some rights-managed or label-encrypted uploads instead produce a generic error.
claims.quote: For some rights-managed or label-encrypted files, the agent returns a generic error instead.

claims.claim: The cited file-input article describes agents powered by the standard harness.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness.

claims.claim: The file-input article directs readers to Microsoft Copilot Chat as an experience supporting sensitivity-labelled files.
claims.quote: use a Microsoft 365 experience such as Microsoft Copilot Chat, which supports sensitivity-labeled files.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams channels make an agent available in Teams and Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: After you publish your agent at least once, you can connect it to the Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams channels so users can chat with it in both Teams and Microsoft Copilot.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: For the documented label-encryption scenario, AI apps need the user's EXTRACT and VIEW rights to return content.
claims.quote: When the sensitivity label applies encryption, users must have the EXTRACT usage right, as well as VIEW, for the AI apps to return the data.

claims.claim: The Purview Copilot Studio page documents encryption support only for sensitivity labels and the SharePoint knowledge source.
claims.quote: Encryption is supported only with sensitivity labels, and only for the SharePoint knowledge source.

claims.claim: The troubleshooting article gives a conflicting description in which encrypted SharePoint knowledge-source content cannot be extracted or grounded.
claims.quote: However, the agent can't extract or ground on content whose protection encrypts the file. This limitation includes sensitivity labels that apply encryption, Double Key Encryption (DKE), and password-protected files.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented upload-specific EXTRACT checks for the planned feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio uploaded files tools connectors sensitivity label EXTRACT DLP enforcement. Opened image-input-analysis, ai-copilot-studio and ai-m365-copilot-considerations; found general EXTRACT rules and existing upload restrictions, not planned upload-specific checks.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Effective EXTRACT permissions can differ from a sensitivity label's configured template permissions.
claims.quote: Copilot and agents honor the EXTRACT usage right for a user, however it was applied to the content. ... there are some situations that can result in the content's usage rights being different from the applied label configuration

claims.where: controls[3].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The person applying encryption is the Rights Management owner and always retains EXTRACT.
claims.quote: The person applying the encryption always has the EXTRACT usage right, because they are the Rights Management owner.

claims.claim: Full control (OWNER) includes EXTRACT.
claims.quote: Because the Full control (OWNER) usage right includes all the usage rights, EXTRACT is automatically included with Full control.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview portal displays EXTRACT as Copy and extract content(EXTRACT).
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, the EXTRACT usage right is displayed as Copy and extract content(EXTRACT).

claims.claim: The label-encryption wizard uses Choose protection settings for the types of items you selected > Control access > Access control > Configure access control settings > Assign permissions now.
claims.quote: on the Choose protection settings for the types of items you selected page, make sure you select Control access. ... On the Access control page ... Configure access control settings ... Assign permissions now

claims.claim: Set-Label supports -Identity <label> -EncryptionEnabled $true -EncryptionProtectionType Template -EncryptionRightsDefinitions <rights>.
claims.quote: The EncryptionRightsDefinitions parameter specifies the rights users have ... This parameter is meaningful only when the EncryptionEnabled parameter value is either $true or $false and the EncryptionProtectionType parameter value is Template.

claims.claim: The printed Set-Label call configures template-based, admin-defined rights rather than user-defined permissions.
claims.quote: The EncryptionProtectionType parameter specifies the protection type for encryption. Valid values are: ... Template ... RemoveProtection ... UserDefined

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Agent flows, connectors and tools can receive uploaded files and pass them to downstream services such as SharePoint or ServiceNow.
claims.quote: Pass files from your Copilot Studio agent to downstream systems using agent flows, connectors, and tools. ... Optionally, you can add logic in your flow to send this file to SharePoint, ServiceNow, Dynamics 365 Customer Service, and similar services.

claims.claim: A sensitivity-label check at the uploaded-file hand-off to flows, connectors or tools is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio uploaded files tools connectors sensitivity label EXTRACT DLP enforcement. Opened pass-files-to-connectors, image-input-analysis and ai-copilot-studio; none documents a label check at the file-to-tool hand-off.

claims.claim: The planned labelled-upload identity model is not documented beyond the roadmap's user/agent account wording.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio uploaded files tools connectors sensitivity label EXTRACT DLP enforcement. Read image-input-analysis, ai-copilot-studio and the roadmap; no upload-specific identity details beyond the roadmap's user/agent account wording.

claims.claim: Copilot and agents have restrictions on unopened SharePoint and OneDrive documents encrypted with user-defined permissions.
claims.quote: Copilot and agents can't access unopened documents in SharePoint and OneDrive when they're labeled and encrypted with user-defined permissions

claims.claim: One exception is a default label extending SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents, with EXTRACT still required.
claims.quote: unless the label is used as a default sensitivity label that extends SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents or they're directly referenced by typing "/" (and in both cases, the user has EXTRACT permissions).

claims.claim: Another exception is directly referencing the document by typing '/', with EXTRACT still required.
claims.quote: or they're directly referenced by typing "/" (and in both cases, the user has EXTRACT permissions).

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisites; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Purview recommends enabling sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive for the documented labelled-content scenario.
claims.quote: If you haven't already, we recommend you enable sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive and also familiarize yourself with the file types and label configurations that these services can process.

claims.claim: Without enabling sensitivity labels for those services, accessible encrypted files are limited to data in use from Office apps on Windows.
claims.quote: When sensitivity labels aren't enabled for these services, the encrypted files that Copilot and agents can access are limited to data in use from Office apps on Windows.

claims.claim: The documented label-based Copilot DLP coverage for Copilot Studio agents is restricted to SharePoint knowledge sources.
claims.quote: When the knowledge source is SharePoint, a DLP policy scoped to the Microsoft 365 Copilot location can restrict agents built in Copilot Studio for Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, and Microsoft 365 Copilot from processing sensitive content based on a specified sensitivity label.
